questions.source_text:
Computer Basics
A computer is an electronic device that accepts data (input), processes it according to instructions (programs), stores it, and produces results (output). Charles Babbage is known as the Father of the
Computer for designing the Analytical Engine in the 1830s.
1. Main Parts of a Computer
• CPU (Central Processing Unit): the "brain" of the computer. It has the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit), which does calculations, and the CU (Control Unit), which directs operations.
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that Charles Babbage is recognized as the ‘Father of the Computer’ due to his design of the Analytical Engine. The other options are components *within* a computer, not the originator of the concept.
The text explicitly states that RAM is ‘temporary (volatile) memory,’ meaning it loses data when power is turned off. The other options describe ROM or storage devices.

questions.source_text:
• Memory: RAM is temporary (volatile) memory that loses data when power is off. ROM is permanent (non-volatile) memory that stores start-up instructions.
• Storage: HDD (hard disk drive), SSD (solid state drive, faster), and pen drives keep data permanently.
• Motherboard: the main circuit board that connects all components.

3. Hardware and Software
Hardware is the physical part of a computer that we can touch. Software is a set of programs that tells the hardware what to do. Software is of two types:
• System software: runs the computer, e.g. Operating Systems such as Windows, Linux, macOS and
Android.
• Application software: does specific tasks, e.g. MS Word, web browsers, games, and calculators.

questions.source_text:
4. Units of Memory
The smallest unit is a bit (0 or 1). 8 bits = 1 Byte; 1024 Bytes = 1 Kilobyte (KB); 1024 KB = 1 Megabyte (MB); 1024 MB = 1 Gigabyte (GB); 1024 GB = 1 Terabyte (TB).
5. Generations of Computers
• First (1940–56): vacuum tubes
• Second (1956–63): transistors
• Third (1964–71): integrated circuits (ICs)
• Fourth (1971–present): microprocessors
• Fifth (present and beyond): artificial intelligence (AI)
6. Important Terms
options: Artificial intelligence is a characteristic of the Fifth generation of computers.
Transistors were used in the Second generation of computers.
